title: Sequential Session ID Generation
pattern: Allocating session cookies or user access identifiers using incremental integers, timestamps, or simple sequential numbers.
why_bad: Enables trivial session hijacking. Attackers can guess or brute-force valid session identifiers of other active users on the system, completely bypassing authentication.
detection: Sequential increments or low-entropy formulas inside methods returning session identifiers.
fix: Generate session keys using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) yielding high-entropy, unpredictable values.
source: `Heather Adkins et al. - Building Secure and Reliable Systems (2020)`, Ch 5, p. 78.
